agree.reason: The letter explains the gap clearly and gives the $38,000-to-$9,000 result, but the owner, who needs someone fast after a two-week departure, gets no start date, no plan for Dentrix and no recent work to reassure him, so he may well stay unsure.

honest.reason: The figures match the brief, but 'led our move' and 'I reduced' are a bit stronger than 'handled', and 'kept daily operations running while staff adjusted' adds detail the brief did not give.

works_the_facts.reason: It gives the raw $38,000-to-$9,000 drop but never calls it a cut of about three-quarters, and it never points out that 4 vets and 14 staff is a larger operation than 3 dentists and 9 staff.

right_comparison.reason: It never compares the clinic she ran with the smaller practice she would manage, which was the obvious way to show she can handle the job.

qualification.reason: The Dentrix hedge rests on an unverifiable 'confident I can learn quickly', when it could have named the 20-hour course she has already signed up for and said she will finish it before her first day.

objections.reason: The gap is met head-on, but the doubts about recent skills, Dentrix readiness and availability are left open even though the church treasurer work in QuickBooks, the course, the two-week start and the evening hours would answer them.

fit.reason: It is a proper cover letter under 300 words, but it leaves placeholders for the names, practice and town even though the user supplied them, so it isn't ready to send.
